capitals.name: Philadelphia
capitals.note: Rule: the city where Congress sat on 1 July of the year. The Second Continental Congress sat in Philadelphia from 4 July 1776, at Baltimore from 20 December 1776 to 27 February 1777, again in Philadelphia from 5 March to 18 September 1777, at Lancaster for one day (27 September 1777), at York from 30 September 1777 to 27 June 1778, and in Philadelphia from 2 July 1778; the Congress of the Confederation sat there from 2 March 1781 to 21 June 1783 (List of capitals page).

capitals.name: Princeton
capitals.note: Nassau Hall, 30 June to 4 November 1783 (the Congress last sat in Philadelphia on 21 June).

capitals.name: Annapolis
capitals.note: Maryland State House, 26 November 1783 to 19 August 1784; the Congress then sat at Trenton from 1 November to 24 December 1784.

capitals.name: New York
capitals.note: New York City Hall from 11 January 1785 to 6 October 1788, then Federal Hall for the United States Congress from 4 March 1789 to 5 December 1790.

capitals.name: Washington, D.C.
capitals.note: The United States Capitol, from 17 November 1800 (Congress last sat in Philadelphia on 14 May 1800; the year 1800 is given to Washington). The British burned the public buildings on 24 August 1814 (War of 1812 page); Congress met in other buildings of the city until 4 March 1819 (List of capitals page).

wars.name: Iraq War
wars.outcome: The invasion began on 20 March 2003; Baghdad fell on 9 April; the Coalition Provisional Authority ruled from 21 April 2003 to 28 June 2004, when it 'formally transferred sovereignty'; US forces were withdrawn on 18 December 2011.
wars.note: An occupation, hatched in the ledger for 2003-2004; the zone list is empty because no land was contested between states.

certainty.note: A war with no agreed boundary: the British-held coast and the western posts moved with the campaigns.

The Treaty of Paris lines are written (Mississippi, 31st parallel) but the northern line was unsurveyed, Spain held the Natchez strip until 1796, the British forts until 1796, the Maine boundary was disputed, and the Louisiana limits with Spain were 'disputed'. The interior was Native land. The 49th-parallel line west of the Lake of the Woods is fixed by the Convention of 1818, in force 30 January 1819 (ledger).

Treaty lines: the 49th parallel (1818), the Adams-Onis line (in force 1821), Webster-Ashburton (1842), the Oregon Treaty (1846), the Rio Grande and the cession (1848), Gadsden (1854). Exceptions kept soft: Maine until 13 October 1842; the Oregon Country while jointly occupied (to 1846); the Nueces-Rio Grande zone in 1845-48.
The Civil War front moved campaign by campaign; the border-state lines and Confederate Arizona were never fixed.
Treaty and territorial lines; the Alaska panhandle boundary with Canada was 'vague and disputed' until the award of 20 October 1903.

The boundaries of the territories are treaty or statute lines; occupations (Cuba, Haiti, the Dominican Republic, Japan, Germany, Iraq) and protections (Greenland, Iceland) are status tints in the ledger, not borders.

notes:
SCOPE AND METHOD. One Cliopatria row, 'United States of America', 73 shapes (1776-2024), 14 pages opened of a 14-page budget (the United States and Territorial evolution articles, the Timeline of United States military operations, and the Treaty of Paris 1783, Revolutionary War, Louisiana Purchase, War of 1812, History of Liberia, Oregon Treaty, Mexican-American War, Civil War, Spanish-American War, Iraq War and Northwest Indian War pages). Every ledger event, keyframe verdict and war cites one of them; where a page gave no date or no land the event carries confidence 1 and says 'page silent'. Only 5 of 73 verdicts are ok (1890, 1905, 1911, 1913, 1914); 68 are adjust; none is wrong.

WHAT CLIOPATRIA DRAWS. Until about 1889 the row draws settled and organised land (the 1890 shape is the first that is whole states), not the sovereignty or treaty extent. The dossier takes the treaty extent as the state's land: each acquisition (Louisiana, Florida, Texas, Oregon, Mexican Cession, Gadsden, Alaska) enters as a whole region on its treaty date, and the 'adjust' corrections add what the row lacks and remove what it draws wrongly. Interior Native-held land inside the treaty lines is therefore drawn as United States land with the caveat that it belonged to nations that am-05 should carry (northwestern-confederacy, the southern nations, the plains and Great Basin peoples); the ledger models the Northwest Indian War as a contest zone, not as a loss. Areas were compared with the infobox 9,833,520 km2 (undated): the row's 2024 shape is 9.44 M km2, ratio 0.96, and the 1890 shape 9.40 M km2; cell-based areas run about 3.5 percent below the polygon areas, so corrected areas were rescaled to Cliopatria's basis.

CLIOPATRIA ROWS DRAWN AS UNITED STATES LAND THAT ARE NOT. Liberia (1822-1847, the American Colonization Society colony; History of Liberia page), cells of Canada in 1776-78 and 1814, Cuba (1898-1902 and 1906-09 occupations), Haiti (1915-34), the Dominican Republic (1916-24), Germany, Austria, Japan and South Korea after 1945, Greenland and Iceland in the Second World War, Vietnam and Cambodia in the Vietnam War years, and Iraq, Iran and Kuwait in 2003-2011. Each is removed in the corrections; all but Vietnam and Cambodia (the Timeline page frames the Vietnam War as military involvement, not occupation, so they are only removed from the 1967 shape) are carried as occupation_* or vassal_* events instead (hatched or tinted, not territory). The Philippines (1898-1946) stay United States land, occupied by Japan 1942-05 to 1945-09 (hatched), with a loss to the Republic of the Philippines in 1946. Cliopatria's 'Saint Kitts' row also draws the US Virgin Islands; American Samoa and the Virgin Islands were missing from the US row (1 cell each) and are added.

DISAGREEMENTS BETWEEN PAGES. Confederacy formed 4 February 1861 (Civil War page) or 8 February 1861 (Territory page). Treaty of Paris 1898 signed 10 December 1898 or in force 11 April 1899 (gain dated 1898-12 to match the spanish-empire dossier). Oregon Treaty 15 June 1846 (Oregon page) or 17 July 1846 (Territory page). Adams-Onis signed 1819 (Louisiana page, spanish-florida dossier) or in force 22 February 1821, with East Florida ceded 10 July and West Florida 17 July 1821 (Territory page). Guadalupe Hidalgo: the war range ends 2 February 1848, the Territory page gives 30 May 1848 for the exchange. New York captured 15 September or November 1776. West Florida (Pearl River strip) 26 September and 10 December 1810. Gadsden 30 June 1854 as the page dates it.

DIFFERENCES FROM OTHER DOSSIERS. spanish-florida's 1810 loss is a wider region than the Baton Rouge district used here, and its 1817-19 First Seminole War contest now has a mirror here (1817-11 to 1819-02; repair pass). The 1812 Mobile gain and the July 1821 Florida gain pair with spanish-florida's 1812 loss and 1821-07 dissolve. spanish-empire also carries the 1795 (Pinckney) and 1821 Florida losses to the United States, while this dossier pairs the 1796 West Florida and 1821 Florida gains with spanish-florida: the same land appears under two counterparts, and the 1795 and 1796 dates differ (treaty year against the withdrawal). The 1898 Treaty of Paris gain agrees with spanish-empire (1898-12); spanish-empire's 1898-12 Cuba loss has no gain here: on this side it is the end of the occupation of Spanish Cuba (repair pass; am-06 should record an end of occupation, not a transfer). republic-of-hawai-i dissolves in 1898-08 and the gain here is 1898-08. united-states-army-military-government-in-korea (ea group, 1945-48) is a separate polity for land this dossier carries as occupation of South Korea 1945-49; one of the two should own the hatching.

NEEDED FROM OTHER STATES. thirteen-colonies (the predecessor; Cliopatria has no row for the colonies after 1713, so the founding year draws no one's land), northwestern-confederacy (am-05; counterpart of the Northwest Indian War contest 1786-1795), first-philippine-republic (counterpart of the 1899 Philippine-American War contest); texas, the Confederacy and Vermont are counterparts that other am-07 parts write.

NOT DRAWN (page silent or over budget). The Trust Territory of the Pacific Islands and the Northern Mariana Islands, 1944/47 to 1986/94 (the Trust Territory page was opened for dates only: UN trusteeship 18 July 1947, US administrations ended 1986, trusteeship ended 22 December 1990 and for Palau 25 May 1994; empire-of-japan records the 1945 transfer as a loss while the US side would be a trusteeship, and four successor dossiers exist, micronesia, republic-of-the-marshall-islands, palau and commonwealth-of-the-northern-mariana-islands, so the typing needs one coordinated pass), the Bonin and Volcano Islands 1945-68 (the Ryukyus page is silent on them), the guano islands, Navassa, the Corn and Swan Islands, the Hawaiian annexation resolution date, the Aroostook War, Mobile in 1813, Native cession treaties, the St. Croix boundary, Indian Stream (assigned to the United States in 1842; not drawn), and the end of the Veracruz and Mexico City occupations (1848, confidence 1: the Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo page also gives no withdrawal date). Rulers now run 1789-2024 (presidents, List of presidents page); 1776-1788 (Presidents of the Congress) is not listed. Capitals follow the List of capitals page (rule: where Congress sat on 1 July of the year).

GAZETTEER NAMES MISSING (polygons, places or unions were used instead). Mexican Cession, Gadsden Purchase, Panama Canal Zone, Guantanamo Bay lease area, Castine, Kaskaskia, Sonoma, Midway Atoll, Wake Island, Alaska Panhandle, Natchez strip (northern West Florida), Nueces strip, Mobile District (Pearl to Perdido), Old Northwest without Minnesota, eastern Maine, Upper Canada Niagara shore. Repair pass names added: northern Maine strip (Aroostook and the upper Saint John valley), Hudson Bay drainage south of 49N (Red River valley and Souris loop), Milk-Poplar-Big Muddy watersheds, Middle Tennessee, West Tennessee, East Tennessee, American sector of the Rhineland.

REPAIR PASS (2026-10-19, after the reviewer's fail verdict). 33 further pages were opened at the reviewer's direction (sources marked 'Repair pass'), beyond the original 14-page budget. Fixes: (1) the 1863 West Virginia gain is deleted and the admission is noted on the 1861-04 loss; (2) the Convention of 1818 is two events of 1819-01 (gain of the Hudson Bay drainage south of 49N; loss of the Milk, Poplar and Big Muddy watersheds), the 1804 Louisiana event and the 1805-1815 keyframes draw the purchase without the first and with the second until then; (3) the Philippines 1942-45 are an occupation by Japan (1942-05 to 1945-09) with new occupation pairs for Guam, Wake, Kiska and Attu, and the 1942 and 1944 keyframes keep the islands; (4) wars: World War II replaces the 1944-1946 reoccupation entry; World War I, the Korean War and the First Seminole War are added; (5) the 1842 Maine gain, the found region and the corrections of 1776-1840 are limited to Maine north of 46N; (6) Tennessee is gained in three steps (Middle 1862-02, West 1862-06, East 1863-09); (7) Midway (1867-08) and Wake (1899-01) are dated gains from nobody; (8) Cuba: the 1898-07 occupation is against spanish-empire and ends 1898-12, a second pair 1898-12 to 1902-05 runs against republic-of-cuba; (9) the seceded states stood alone from 1860-12 to February 1861 (flag for am-07 part d); (10) Korea and Germany name their 1945 owners (empire-of-japan, nazi-germany); (11) the Revolutionary War starts in 1776. Folded in from the thin list: Georgia contest end 1782-07, Trans-Mississippi 1865-06, Philippine-American War start 1899-02, Greenland and Iceland ends, Canal Zone 1979-10, capitals, presidents, the Rhineland 1918-12 to 1923-01, Okinawa and Amami, and mirrors of the Sullivan Expedition, the 31N-32 28N strip and the First Seminole War. Choices and disagreements: Convention of 1818 dated 1819-01 (in force; signed 20 October 1818); East Tennessee dated 1863-09 (Knoxville campaign page) not 1863-11, because the November battles lifted a siege and did not change who held the city; the Cuba occupation restarts in 1898-12, not 1899-01, because no page opened dates the Spanish evacuation; the Korean occupation ends 1948-08 (military government) not 1949 (troops out); Greenland's protection ends 1945-05 (return to Copenhagen) rather than 1951 (base treaty replaced the agreement); Webster-Ashburton is dated by the Territory page (13 October 1842), the Webster-Ashburton page gives the signing as 9 August 1842; Midway and Wake resolve to zero Cliopatria cells, so they are in the ledger but not added to the keyframes.
